title: Urban Growth Boundary — Core Overview (Edition 1)
description: An urban growth boundary draws a legal line around a metro area, concentrating development inside and preserving farmland and open space outside. Oregon's 1973 statewide planning law required every city to adopt one, with Portland's boundary the best-known example. This overview edition presents Urban Growth Boundary as a core land-use concept for contemporary cities.

real_examples.fact: Portland's urban growth boundary, established under Oregon's 1973 land-use law, is expanded only after the region demonstrates land need.
